claims.text: The GPS trace, not the rounded trip_record copy, governs the threshold test: POL-RD-01 says so in terms. The trace runs 10.78 km between the recorded pickup and the recorded dropoff against a booked optimal of 7.2 km — an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass comfortably: far more than 20% of optimal, and far more than the 0.8 km absolute floor. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The fare is metered, so the refund is arithmetic rather than discretionary and POL-RD-02 governs. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.0, read from the fare_breakdown itself. This is not an upfront-quoted trip, so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-and-time route.

Running POL-RD-02 on the booked optimal route: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 7.2 km + 0.28 x 19.0 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = 14.52 + 0.80 = 15.32. Charged_total is 26.04. Refund = 26.04 - 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 10.75. That is 41% of the charge, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not a full one, and it is well above the 0.50 de minimis floor.

The two ERP gantries the rider is disputing are off the optimal corridor and are already paid for inside that 10.75. The optimal route is a no-gantry route — trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00 — while the fare_breakdown charges $3.00 at CTE Braddell Rd and $2.50 at the CTE Chin Swee tunnel, both itemised on_optimal_route false: $5.50 the rider would never have paid. Under POL-RD-09(1) this pass-through is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, because the recomputed fare includes only on-optimal-route gantries; it is itemised for transparency and must not be added on top of the 10.75.

No road-closure exoneration under POL-RD-03 is available to the driver. The only traffic-advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00106-01, is MISSING, has no payload and carries weight 0.0; its own issue detail records that no LTA advisory covers Thomson Rd, the CTE or the Chin Swee tunnel in the 08:29-09:03 window on 17 July 2026. I disclose that this artifact is impaired at weight 0.0 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) — its value to the rider's case is precisely its absence, which is itself citable, and there is nothing for POL-RD-03 to attach to.

Nor can the detour be pinned on the rider under POL-RD-04. The chat log contains exactly one message, from the rider, timed 08:46:30: 'why we at havelock? bugis is behind us'. That is a complaint about the route, not an instruction to take it, and no instruction or admission appears anywhere in the log. Its waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run at all and the clause is unavailable. No rider-caused detour reduces the excess.

There was no relocation of either endpoint under POL-RD-05: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip_record, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null with them. The 7.2 km booked optimal is therefore the correct baseline and no distance is excluded on this ground.

This is not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 gives the driver no matched-itinerary baseline to hide behind. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL; the 7.2 km figure is the platform optimal for this rider's own itinerary and is the comparator POL-RD-01 requires.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 burden on both limbs. The artifacts describe the same trip — trip_id TRP-00106 and the pickup timestamp match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown — and the excess of 3.58 km (49.72%) meets the POL-RD-01 threshold. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07: 100% coverage, 169 fixes, a 10 s sampling interval against a 10 s expected interval, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so neither limb (a), (b) nor (c) fires and no independent corroboration is required.

The rider-side corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 does not bite. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-or-more that would demand corroboration beyond the trace, and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1. The rider's claim is proven on the trace and needs nothing further.

The driver_profile check that POL-RD-06 requires produces no repeat-deviation pattern, and the rider does not ask for the uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and 0 divided by 96 completed trips is below the 0.05 ratio, so limb (b) of POL-RD-06 adds nothing to the POL-RD-02 figure. The rider rests on this trip's own trace for the finding, as POL-GEN-01 requires, and asks only for the 10.75 the arithmetic yields.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, and this case can and should be decided on the money. TRP-00106 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; the refund of 10.75 is far below the SGD 150 cap and below charged_total; and both ERP lines are matched to the trace, the nearest fix being 0 m from the Braddell Rd gantry and 24.1 m from the Chin Swee tunnel gantry, well inside POL-RD-09's 250 m crossing tolerance. There is a determinate monetary answer here, and it is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 10.75 to the rider.

claims.text: The governing distance figure is the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded convenience copy: under POL-RD-01 the trace measures 10.78 km against a booked optimal of 7.2 km, an excess of 3.58 km, which is 49.72% of optimal. That clears the 20% / 0.8 km establishment gate but falls below the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gate, so this is an established but NON-MATERIAL deviation, not the runaway detour the claim text describes.

Because the deviation is not material, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable; the rider's remedy is confined to the POL-RD-02 arithmetic partial refund and cannot be escalated to the whole contested amount.

Even if the driver's profile were consulted, the POL-RD-06 pattern test fails on its own terms: deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 96, a ratio of 0.000, far under the 0.05 threshold and under the absolute threshold of 3 flags. No pattern is established, so there is no uplift and no conduct referral; POL-GEN-01 confines this artifact to that single test and nothing else on the profile may ground a finding.

The rider's demand for the $5.50 of ERP on top of the distance refund double-counts. Under POL-RD-09(1) a POL-RD-02 refund already comprehends off-route ERP, because the recomputed fare counts only gantries lying on the optimal route - here none, since both charged gantries carry on_optimal_route false and the booked optimal route's own ERP is 0.00. Off-route ERP must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure.

Both ERP lines are genuine crossings and not phantom charges: the nearest trace fixes lie 0.0 m and 24.1 m from the two gantry coordinates, inside the 250 m match tolerance in POL-RD-09, so each line is matched to the trace. No standalone billing-integrity refund arises under POL-RD-09(4).

The driver has no exculpatory clause on this record and I do not stretch for one: the traffic advisory is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, severity BLOCKING), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run; the chat log holds a single unanswered rider question with waypoint_hint null, so POL-RD-04's waypoint corroboration test is undecidable and that clause is unavailable; and the trip record shows no amended endpoints, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. The deviation therefore stands, but only to the extent of the POL-RD-02 arithmetic.

The ceiling on any refund is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic: charged_total of 26.04 less a recomputed fare of ((3.80 + 0.75 x 7.2 + 0.28 x 19.0) x the 1.0 surge on the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 of on-optimal-route ERP = 15.32, giving 10.72 rounded up to SGD 10.75. That figure - not the $16.25 of distance refund plus $5.50 ERP, and not the full $26.04 - is the most the rider can recover on this record.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is for both parties.

WHAT HAPPENED. The trace governs the threshold test (POL-RD-01), not the trip record's rounded copy:
• actual (gps_trace.trace_distance_km): 10.78 km
• optimal (trip_record, booked): 7.2 km
• excess: 3.58 km = 49.72% of optimal

That clears both establishment gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does NOT clear the materiality gate, which needs more than 50% or more than 8.0 km — 49.72% is just under 50% and 3.58 km is under 8.0 km. The rider's description of a runaway detour is therefore overstated in degree, though the deviation itself is real; the driver's route was longer than the booked optimal and was not excused.

NO EXONERATION. The driver has no clause that excuses the excess. The only traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-00106-01) is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT (BLOCKING) — nothing covers Thomson Rd, the CTE or the Chin Swee tunnel in the trip window — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run. The chat log holds one rider complaint at 08:46:30 ('why we at havelock? bugis is behind us'), not an instruction, and its waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and that clause is unavailable. There was no endpoint amendment (POL-RD-05) and the vehicle is RYDE_TAXI, not a pooled RYDE_POOL trip (POL-RD-12), so the 7.2 km booked optimal is the correct baseline.

THE REFUND (POL-RD-02, metered fare, surge 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown):
• charged_total: 26.04
• recomputed_fare: (3.80 + 0.75 × 7.2 + 0.28 × 19.0) × 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-optimal-route ERP = 15.32
• refund: 26.04 − 15.32 = 10.72, rounded UP to 10.75

That is ~41% of the charge, so PARTIAL_REFUND, above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and far below the POL-RD-10(6) cap.

ERP — NOT ADDED ON TOP. The rider asks for the $5.50 of ERP in addition to the distance refund. That would double-count. Both charged gantries (CTE Braddell Rd $3.00, CTE Chin Swee tunnel $2.50) are off the optimal corridor (on_optimal_route false) and the optimal route itself carries 0.00 ERP, so under POL-RD-09(1) they are already comprehended inside the 15.32 recomputed fare and the 10.75 refund. They are itemised here only for transparency and are never added to it. Both lines are genuine crossings, matched to the trace at 0.0 m and 24.1 m — inside POL-RD-09's 250 m tolerance — so no standalone billing-integrity refund arises under POL-RD-09(4) and no referral is produced. The rider's '$16.25 + $5.50' figure and the full $26.04 claim are both rejected on that ground.

NO DRIVER-SIDE UPLIFT OR REFERRAL. Because the deviation is non-material, the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged, and in any event it fails on its own terms: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 96 completed_trips_90d, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no conduct referral is produced. The profile artifacts were used only for the tests the policy names and for nothing else (POL-GEN-01).

NO ESCALATION. TRP-00106 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 169 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0); timestamps agree; the refund is under both caps; and both ERP lines have counterparts in the trace. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and this case is decided on the money.

RESULT. The rider is refunded SGD 10.75 and the remaining charge stands; the driver is not fined and no driver compensation is due (no unbilled distance appears — billed 10.8 km against a 10.78 km trace). Confidence 0.92; the deciding facts rest on artifacts of weight 1.0 (gps_trace, trip_record, fare_breakdown, chat_log), so nothing caps the ruling below the 0.70 floor.
